title: Your Brain Can't Feel Pain (That's Why Surgery Can Be Awake)

scenes.text: Your brain cannot feel pain. Not even when a surgeon cuts into it.
In awake brain surgery, the patient talks, counts and moves while the surgeon works inside their head.
They may feel pressure, maybe some pulling. But no pain from the brain itself.
Surgeons do it on purpose, so they can map which spots control speech or movement, and steer around them.
It works because the brain has no pain receptors. It reads pain signals from everywhere else, but it has none of its own.
So where do headaches come from? Blood vessels, muscles and the membranes around your brain. Never the brain itself.

description:
Your brain cannot feel pain, which is why some brain surgery is done while the patient is awake, talking and counting.
The brain has no pain receptors of its own. It processes pain signals from the rest of the body, but cutting into it doesn't hurt. Patients may feel pressure or pulling, but the scalp is numbed.
Headaches come from blood vessels, muscles and the membranes around the brain, not the brain itself.
Would you stay awake for brain surgery?
